claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. 

To get started, I need to gather some information about your situation. Let me begin with a basic question:

**What is the name of the child or children you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm looking to claim for my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that context. So you're looking to claim Child Benefit for your son **Alex**.

To assess your eligibility, I need to understand more about Alex's circumstances. Let me start with this question:

**How old is Alex, or what is his date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. So Alex is 8 years old.

Now, to continue assessing your eligibility, I need to know:

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you for confirming that Alex lives with you.

Now I need to gather some more information about your circumstances:

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming you live in the UK.

I need to ask a bit more specifically about your immigration status to properly assess your eligibility:

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status (Indefinite Leave to Remain) in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for clarifying that.

Now I have one more important question about your residency:

**Have you lived in the UK for at least 2 of the last 3 years?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that confirmation.

Just to make sure I have all the information I need, let me ask:

**Is Alex in full-time education, or does he have any conditions that would affect his eligibility (such as being in hospital or care)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, he's been in hospital for a few months now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know that Alex has been in hospital for a few months. This is important information.

To better understand his situation:

**Is Alex still currently in hospital, or has he been discharged?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's still in hospital, yes.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that Alex is still in hospital.

I need to understand a bit more about his hospital stay:

**Are you still responsible for Alex's maintenance and upbringing while he's in hospital, or is the hospital covering his costs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, I haven't really been able to spend money on him while he's been in there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Let me ask this more clearly:

**Does the hospital provide Alex with food, accommodation, and other essentials while he's an inpatient, or are you still paying for his care and upkeep?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: The hospital is providing everything - food, accommodation, all of that. I haven't been spending money on his needs while he's there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the guidance on this to ensure I'm giving you the correct assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided and the government guidance I've reviewed, I can now give you my assessment.

I can see that Alex has been in hospital for a few months. According to the Child Benefit rules, your entitlement is affected if your child is in hospital for more than 12 weeks. Since you've confirmed that:
- The hospital is providing all of Alex's food, accommodation, and essentials
- You haven't been spending money on his needs while he's there
- He's been in hospital for "a few months" (which appears to be less than 12 weeks based on your description)

However, I need one clarification to give you a definitive answer:

**Approximately how many weeks has Alex been in hospital - is it less than 12 weeks, or has it been 12 weeks or longer?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been about 15 weeks now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying. Based on all the information you've provided, I can now give you my final assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Summary

Unfortunately, **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

While you meet all the basic requirements (you're a British citizen, you've lived in the UK for at least 2 of the last 3 years, and Alex is your child under 16), your eligibility has been affected by Alex's hospital stay.

**The key issue:** Alex has been in hospital for 15 weeks, which exceeds the 12-week limit. Since the hospital is providing all of his food, accommodation, and essentials, and you're not regularly spending money on his maintenance while he's an inpatient, you are no longer entitled to Child Benefit under the rules.

**What you should do:**
- Contact HMRC to inform them of this change in circumstances
- If Alex is discharged and returns home, or if you begin regularly spending money on his maintenance while in hospital, your eligibility may be reinstated
- HMRC can advise you on any exceptions that might apply to your specific situation

I'm sorry to hear about Alex's situation, and I hope he recovers well.

According to the Child Benefit rules, when a child is in hospital or residential accommodation for more than 12 weeks, and the hospital is providing all the child's food, accommodation, and essentials (meaning you are not regularly spending money on them), you are no longer entitled to Child Benefit after the 12-week limit has been reached. Since Alex has now exceeded the 12-week threshold and you are not spending money on his maintenance while he is an inpatient, you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex at this time.
